decode_concurrency_with_mtp_20260921.question: does the 2.5x aggregate from four streams (2026-09-18, speculation off) stack with MTP speculation, which already verifies 4 tokens per pass?
decode_concurrency_with_mtp_20260921.method: tools/decode_concurrency.py --n 128 on the production build (bin/hip-rocm101), server started by tools/manager.py with profile {parallel: 4, context: 65536} - everything else the default: MTP on with the shared-Q4_K_M-head-iq4_xs draft, draft_max 3, QSA on, vision on, 96 GB carve, dedicated memory (unified=False). Short prompts, so attention/KV cost is negligible and this is the ceiling. Per-stream figures are the server's predicted_per_token_ms; 'sum' adds the streams' rates, 'wall' is tokens over wall-clock including prompt processing.

1 stream after.note: no thermal drift after the four-stream burst

decode_concurrency_with_mtp_20260921.reading: 1.54x at four streams with MTP (37.5 -> 57.7) against 2.5x without it (19.0 -> 47.1). Both are the same lever - weight bytes read once per step shared by more tokens - and MTP had already taken most of it: a single stream verifies 4 tokens per pass, so four streams make a 16-token verify. A 4-token pass costs ~64 ms and a 16-token pass ~167 ms (69.4 ms/token x 2.4 accepted tokens per pass): 4x the tokens for 2.6x the time, which is close to bandwidth-linear because on a MoE the routed experts touched grow with the batch and only the trunk, attention and shared expert are read once.
decode_concurrency_with_mtp_20260921.load_limit: -np 4 fails to load at context 262144 (ROCm 'unspecified launch failure' at ~38 s, during the projector upload, i.e. a sticky error from the graph reserve; reproducible three times, also with unified memory, not memory pressure). Loads at 131072 and 65536. Bisected at 32768: MTP off, vision off, block-key cache off, decode gather off, QSA off and -np 2 all load, so the failure is the combination of four slots and the 262144 reserve, not one of the optimisations. DIAGNOSED (same day): HIP_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 shows PAL 'failed to submit CMD' while the draft model loads. The mixed-sequence reserve (any parallel > 1) keeps a dense f16 KQ mask of n_ctx x ubatch, exactly 4 GiB at 262144 x 8192, which the driver will not fill: -np 2 fails the same way, -np 4 with ubatch 4096 (2 GiB) loads. But with the ubatch reduced to 7936 the first mixed prefill at 262144 still dies in a MUL_MAT ('unspecified launch failure' at the first four requests), while 131072 loads and serves four streams (12-14 tok/s each, 51 aggregate at 64 tokens). So the manager refuses parallel > 1 above 131072 (error multi_slot_context) rather than pretending.

decode_concurrency_8_slots_mtp_on_off_20.question: the expert-set model (512 experts, 10 per token, ~116 MB each: a batch of n tokens touches 512*(1-(502/512)^n) distinct experts) says the aggregate keeps rising with streams and that MTP's draft tokens compete with real users' tokens for the same expert bytes. Both testable at 8 slots.
decode_concurrency_8_slots_mtp_on_off_20.method: same as above with profile {parallel: 8, context: 65536} and mtp true / false; streams 1, 4, 8; 128 tokens each; the default server was restored afterwards.
decode_concurrency_8_slots_mtp_on_off_20.fit: speculation off: step = ~30 ms fixed + ~1.0 ms per distinct expert touched (116 MB at ~110-116 GB/s). Predicts 40 / 69 / 106 ms for 1 / 4 / 8 tokens against 39.9 / 66.6 / 112.1 measured. The 96 GB carve is why the single-token step is 40 ms here and was 50 ms on 2026-09-18 at 64 GB.
reading: MTP saturates at four streams: 62.4 sum at 4, 62.9 at 8. A 32-token verify is all expert bandwidth (238 distinct experts, ~27 GB per pass), so more streams only make each user slower (8 tok/s each).

MTP and concurrency compete for the same expert budget, and draft tokens are only 60-70% useful: at 8 streams MTP off wins, 71.4 against 62.9; at 4 they tie (60 vs 62); at 1 MTP wins by half (37 vs 25). The crossover is around four users.
Highest aggregate measured on this machine: 71.4 tok/s, 8 streams, speculation off, 8.9 tok/s per user - 2.85x the single-stream no-MTP rate, 1.9x the single-stream MTP rate.

The expert path streams at ~110 GB/s against ~210-220 achievable on this memory: at batch 8 each of the ~76 experts sees about one token, i.e. 76 x 3 small matrix-vector launches. That kernel-side gap, not bandwidth, is the remaining lever for concurrency, and it would help the single stream too.
decode_concurrency_8_slots_mtp_on_off_20.decision: default stays -np 1 with MTP on. For a multi-user deployment: 4 slots either way; beyond 4, MTP off. The multi-stream QSA work (mixed-sequence ubatches on the sparse decode path) is only worth doing for long-context multi-user use, and its ceiling is this ~1.5-1.9x.

expert_path_iq3s_mmq_20260921.question: where the expert kernels actually stand against the memory ceiling, and what of it is kernel rather than bytes
expert_path_iq3s_mmq_20260921.method: tests/test-backend-ops perf -o MUL_MAT_ID with STRIX_MOE_PERF (patch apply_iq3s_mmq_hip adds this model's shapes: 512 experts, 10 used, 640x2560 gate/up and 2560x640 down), GB/s = expected distinct experts touched (512*(1-(502/512)^n)) x expert bytes / time. n=1 and n=4 figures exceed DRAM bandwidth: the working set (7-36 MB) sits in the MALL between repetitions, so only n >= 8 is a DRAM number. In-situ check: STRIX_NODE_TIMING=1 GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1 on real decode steps (tmp captures, not kept).
what_changed: IQ3_S MMQ tile loader on HIP: __vcmpne4/__vsub4 were byte loops (the mmvq vec-dot had already replaced them); sign bytes now come from two multiplies, +20% at 8-16 tokens
the IQ3_S grid is copied into LDS after the x tile: neutral within noise (the 2 KB table was L0-resident anyway), kept because it costs nothing

the fork's compact routed MoE MMQ path (mul_mat_q_routed_compact, RDNA3.5, 512 experts) was gated to IQ4_NL; opened to IQ3_S and IQ4_XS: the 24+ token cliff (73 GB/s) is gone, 156-173 GB/s to 64 tokens

decode_ab.method: tmp/decode_ab.py: production runtime against the build, same manager argv, 128 tokens per stream, short prompts, 96 GB carve

np1 mtp 1 stream.read: unchanged: a 4-token verify goes through mmvq, not MMQ

np4 mtp 4 streams.read: within the acceptance noise (prod's two runs differ by 15%)

np8 mtp 8 streams.read: +16%: the 32-token verify was on the cliff

expert_path_iq3s_mmq_20260921.reading: In the production configuration (one user, MTP, 4-7 tokens per verify) the expert kernels were already near the ceiling - the earlier '110 GB/s' came from attributing every per-token cost to the experts; the per-token costs that actually grow with the batch are the GDN state traffic (fp32 recurrent state, ~3 MB per sequence per layer, read and written every step), the PLE gather, and the per-token projections. What was kernel-bound was IQ3_S in MMQ (the multi-user regime) and the tiling cliff above 16 tokens; both are fixed. The remaining IQ3_S gap to IQ4_NL (157 vs ~190) is the format's unpacking, not memory.
not_done: GDN recurrent state in bf16 instead of fp32 would halve the per-sequence traffic that makes 8 streams cost 15 ms per step in GATED_DELTA_NET; numerics untested
tried_and_dropped: mmvq IQ3_S vec-dot with one dp4a per word (signed bytes by xor+add) instead of the two the sign split needs: 913/913 correct, no change at n=1/4/8 (295/332/150 GB/s-equivalent against 282-336 before). The cache-hot n<=4 figures already exceed DRAM bandwidth, so the single user's gate/up kernels are memory-bound as they stand; the 15% per-byte gap to IQ4_NL on a hot cache does not reach the wall clock. Reverted.

gdn_state_bf16_20260921.question: the GDN recurrent state (128x128 per head, 48 heads, 36 layers: 3.1 MB per sequence per layer, gathered by get_rows, read and rewritten by the kernel, copied back as snapshots) is 15 ms of GATED_DELTA_NET plus 7.6 ms of GET_ROWS in an eight-user step; does keeping it in bf16 (the state cache dtype vLLM uses) buy any of that back?
gdn_state_bf16_20260921.method: recurrent_type_v BF16 behind STRIX_GDN_STATE_BF16 in llama-model.cpp (get_rows widens to f32 for the kernel, the snapshot copy narrows; the CUDA scale op taught bf16 so ggml_scale_inplace(state, 0) can zero a new sequence's row), built to build/bin, A/B against the production runtime with tmp/decode_ab.py.
gdn_state_bf16_20260921.reading: nothing, at any stream count. The state's DRAM traffic was not what those 22 ms were: the f32 intermediate get_rows writes and the kernel reads is MALL-resident (25 MB for eight sequences against a 32 MB last-level cache), and the kernel itself runs at ~120 GB/s-equivalent because of how it walks the state, not because of how many bytes the state has. Halving the stored bytes changed neither. Reverted; a faster GDN kernel would be a kernel rewrite (coalescing and occupancy on the per-head 64 KB state), worth up to ~10 ms of an eight-user step and ~1 ms of a one-user one.
gdn_state_bf16_20260921.not_verified: numerics of bf16 state were not evaluated since there was nothing to keep

draft_budget_20260921.question: a per-step draft budget shared by the drafting slots (STRIX_SPEC_BUDGET=4: one slot 3, two slots 2 each, three or four 1, more than four none) - does 'fewer draft tokens per user under load' beat the fixed draft of 3?
draft_budget_20260921.method: server-side patch in the drafting loop (n_max trimmed per slot, slots with a zero share skip drafting and catch up later), built to build/bin, A/B against the production runtime (fixed draft 3), -np 8 in both so only the stream count changes, 128 tokens per stream.
draft_budget_20260921.reading: no gain that survives the noise (+5% at two streams, -6% at four, -3% at eight, run-to-run spread of the same size). With apply_iq3s_mmq_hip the fixed draft of 3 is no longer worse than no draft at eight streams (71.8 against 72.7), so the earlier 'past four users turn MTP off' no longer holds either - it was a symptom of the 24+ token cliff. Dropped; the fixed draft of 3 stays at every stream count.

prompt_cache_disk_20260921.question: how much of a returning conversation's prefill can a disk cache save on this model, and is a restored state faithful?
prompt_cache_disk_20260921.state_size: 30.5 KB per token: a 34K-token session is 1.06 GB of state plus 113 MB per recurrent checkpoint (one every 8192 prompt tokens), 1.3-1.7 GB on disk
prompt_cache_disk_20260921.slot_save_restore_alone: the /slots save and restore endpoints carry the state (0.9 s to write, 0.5 s to read) but not the checkpoints, and a hybrid model cannot resume without one: the next turn was re-processed in full (38 s) - 'forcing full prompt re-processing due to lack of cache data'
prompt_cache_disk_20260921.disk_tier: patch apply_prompt_cache_disk: every RAM prompt-cache entry (tokens, state, checkpoints) is also written under STRIX_PROMPT_CACHE_DIR; a RAM miss is looked up on disk with the RAM cache's own prefix criteria. tmp/prompt_cache_probe.py: two 34K sessions alternating on one slot - first turns 38.5 / 37.5 s (33911 tokens), second turns 341 / 353 ms (14 tokens, RAM tier); server restarted, third turns 648 / 628 ms (13 / 50 tokens, read from disk in 1.45 / 1.22 s) against 38.9 s from scratch
prompt_cache_disk_20260921.faithfulness: greedy strings differed between a from-scratch run and the cached paths, so the first token's log-probabilities were compared instead (tmp/state_probs_probe.py): live slot, RAM-cache restore and disk-cache restore are identical to three decimals (top-5: -0.000, -13.297, -14.544, -15.037, -17.252); the from-scratch run differs (-0.000, -10.945, -11.506, -11.671, -11.772) with the same top token. The restore is exact; what differs is processing the last 13 tokens as a 14-token batch against inside an 8192-token prefill batch - the batch-size numerics this codebase has always had. So a cached conversation continues exactly as it would have on its own slot.
prompt_cache_disk_20260921.manager: profile prompt_cache_disk (default on), config/jan/prompt-cache, PROMPT_CACHE_DISK_MIB 16384, oldest first; Configuration page switch 'Keep conversation state on disk'

multi_slot_memory_20260921.question: what more than one slot costs in GPU memory at the context it is allowed (131072), and what the ubatch does to it
multi_slot_memory_20260921.method: GPU Adapter Memory counters (dedicated + shared) read right after the load, before any request, so the lazily mapped weights are untouched and the difference is the reserve; then one 34.6K-token prefill per ubatch with four slots
multi_slot_memory_20260921.reading: four slots at ubatch 8192 cost ~8.7 GB over one slot (the mixed-sequence reserve: dense f16 mask of n_ctx x ubatch plus the dense per-block bias, both scaling with the ubatch), almost all of it landing in shared memory. ubatch 2048 brings that to ~1.6 GB and eight slots cost no more than four, at 18% of prefill throughput (873 -> 717 t/s) and with a prefill chunk of 2.9 s instead of 9.4 s between other slots' decode steps. The root - the sparse attention path declining mixed-sequence ubatches so the reserve assumes dense - is the multi-stream QSA work not undertaken. Defaults unchanged: ubatch 8192; a multi-agent deployment that cares about the 7 GB or the interleave should set ubatch 2048 on the Configuration page's advanced section.

full_context.np4 ctx 262144 ubatch 2048: loads in 37 s; four streams 42.3 tok/s (64-token runs); 34636-token prefill 48.0 s = 722 t/s; after load dedicated 78.7 GB, shared 7.2 GB
full_context.np4 ctx 262144 ubatch 4096: loads in 45 s; four streams 43.2 tok/s; prefill 45.3 s = 765 t/s; dedicated 79.0 GB, shared 10.2 GB
full_context.reading: the full context is available to several slots; what has to give is the ubatch. The dense mask works at 2 GiB (131072 x 8192, 262144 x 4096) and not at 3.9 (262144 x 7936) or 4 GiB (262144 x 8192), so the manager's rule is now 2 x context x ubatch <= 2 GiB (error multi_slot_ubatch names the ubatch to set) instead of a context cap.

multi_stream_long_context_20260921.question: what several slots cost at long context today, where a mixed-sequence ubatch takes the dense attention path (qsa_scalar_visibility requires one sequence per ubatch; the decode gather requires n_stream == 1 and a single sequence), against one stream at the same depth on the sparse gather path
multi_stream_long_context_20260921.method: tmp/mstream_longctx_probe.py 4096 4 30000: -np 4, ctx 262144, ubatch 4096, unified KV, MTP draft 3, production runtime; four ~34.9K-token prefixes (docs/*.md repeated, distinct header per stream) prefilled one at a time into four slots, then 64-token greedy decodes with cache_prompt so only the question is re-processed; short-context runs on the same server first

long_context_34.9K_per_stream.4 streams: 95-101 ms/token per stream, 28.3 tok/s aggregate (256 tokens in 9.1 s)
long_context_34.9K_per_stream.1 stream afterwards: 31.2 ms/token, i.e. ~8% slower than before the mixed decodes - the block-key cache is probably invalidated by a mixed-sequence step the way an image invalidates it; not chased

multi_stream_long_context_20260921.reading: at long context concurrency is negative today: four users at 35K each get 28 tok/s together, less than one user alone (32), and each waits 99 ms per token instead of 29. The short-context four-stream figure (47 tok/s here, 58 at ctx 65536) is what the same four users would get if their attention stayed sparse, because attention is the only per-token cost that grows with the depth; that gap - 1.7-2x aggregate and a third of the latency at four users, 22 -> ~40 tok/s at two - is what a multi-stream (mixed-sequence) QSA path would return, on top of removing the dense mask reserve (2 GiB at ubatch 4096, 8 GB at 8192), the 2 GiB ubatch rule and the multi-slot prefill loss (765 -> 873 t/s). It would not move the single-user number or the expert-bandwidth ceiling of ~60-70 tok/s aggregate.

multi_stream_qsa_20260921.change: patches/apply_multi_stream_qsa.py (fork commit 72cce52): mixed-sequence ubatches take the sparse path

what_was_wrong.gap_check: the block-key cache gap check compared a ubatch first token position with its last token position as if they were one sequence; a multi-stream decode step tripped it, the flag is sticky, and the cache stayed off for every stream (every block key rebuilt each step: ROPE 5.7 ms and GET_ROWS over the pool per target graph, single stream 28.9 -> 31.2 ms/token afterwards)
what_was_wrong.gather_limit: the decode gather took at most 8 queries; a 4-stream verify step has 16, so it ran dense attention over the whole used pool with the mask (FLASH_ATTN_EXT 40 ms per target graph at 4 x 35K, graphs off)
what_was_wrong.gather_traffic: ggml_get_rows only returns f32, so each gathered f16 row was written as f32, read back and cast: twice the bytes
what_was_wrong.reserve: a mixed ubatch was never scalar, so its graph - the reserve graph included - carried a dense f16 mask of n_kv x n_tokens and a f32 block bias of n_blocks x n_tokens: 3 GB at 262144 x 4096, and the 4 GiB mask at 8192 the driver would not fill

what_changed.gather: one gather and one flash-attention call per layer with every query on the kernel sequence axis (ne[3]), f16 rows through a GET_ROWS node built with an f16 destination (the CUDA kernel already casts to whatever the destination is); limit 32 queries
what_changed.mixed_compact: qsa_scalar_visibility accepts several sequences (one per token, no image or gap in the cache); set_input_qsa_impl fills two membership inputs, seq_blk [n_seqs_unq, n_blocks] and seq_tok [n_seqs_unq, n_tokens]; qwen4exp_apply_compact_visibility multiplies them (seq_blk^T seq_tok, exactly 0/1) into the visibility, so mixed decode and mixed prefill take the compact, maskless path; dirty_max grows with the sequence count
what_changed.manager: the multi_slot_ubatch rule is gone (no dense mask to size); image input requires a single slot (vision_single_slot), because an image needs the ranked block enumeration, which only a single-sequence cache gets - with two conversations resident an image aborts the server in set_input_qsa (oor)
